# nonUi

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a Ui object.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonUi() — Checks whether a value is **not** a Ui object. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/ui</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonUi<T>(value: T | GoogleAppsScript.Base.Ui): value is T;
```

`nonUi(value)` is the same test as `!isUi(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard reads the tag the object reports for itself: `value.toString() === "Ui"`. A plain object that reports the same tag passes too, which in practice means a test double.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type                            | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------------------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| GoogleAppsScript.Base.Ui` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a Ui object; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const ui = SpreadsheetApp.getUi();

nonUi({}); // => true
nonUi(null); // => true
nonUi(ui); // => false
```
